config.title: Lippincott Path Ch8 – Environmental & Nutritional Pathology
config.subtitle: Environmental exposures, occupational hazards, nutritional deficiencies, and metabolic effects of toxic agents

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man presents with a 6-week history of increasing fatigue and dark-colored stools. Complete blood count shows hemoglobin of 8.6 g/dL and microcytic, hypochromic RBCs. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals a peptic ulcer along the lesser curvature of the stomach. This patient's anemia is most likely caused by deficiency of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage from a peptic ulcer causes ongoing loss of heme iron at a rate faster than it can be replaced from dietary sources, resulting in iron-deficiency anemia. The hallmark laboratory findings are microcytic (small) and hypochromic (pale) red blood cells, reflecting reduced hemoglobin synthesis due to insufficient iron for heme production. Folic acid (A) and vitamin B12 (D) deficiencies produce macrocytic (large cell) anemia, not microcytic. Dark stools (melena) indicate upper GI bleeding.
keypoints: ⭐ Iron deficiency from GI blood loss produces microcytic, hypochromic anemia
Dark/tarry stools (melena) indicate upper GI bleeding (proximal to ligament of Treitz)
⭐ Folic acid and B12 deficiencies cause macrocytic anemia, not microcytic
Iron is required for heme synthesis; deficiency limits hemoglobin production

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man presents for a routine physical examination, which demonstrates an enlarged liver. During the visit, he describes memos from his supervisor at work regarding chronic exposure to vinyl chloride. The patient has an elevated risk for which of the following tumors?
questions.explanation: Occupational exposure to vinyl chloride, used in the production of plastics (polyvinyl chloride, PVC), is associated with the development of angiosarcoma of the liver—a malignant tumor of hepatic endothelial cells. This is also associated with exposure to arsenic (in pesticides) and Thorotrast (a radioactive contrast medium). Hepatic adenoma (C) is associated with oral contraceptive use, not vinyl chloride. The other choices have no known association with vinyl chloride exposure.
keypoints: ⭐ Vinyl chloride (PVC production) → hepatic angiosarcoma
Other causes of hepatic angiosarcoma: arsenic and Thorotrast
⭐ Hepatic adenoma is associated with oral contraceptive use, not vinyl chloride
Angiosarcoma is a malignant tumor of vascular endothelial cells

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with longstanding Crohn disease and severe fat malabsorption experiences a fracture of the femoral neck after a minor contusion. This woman most likely has a deficiency of which of the following vitamins?
questions.explanation: Fat malabsorption from longstanding Crohn disease impairs absorption of all fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K). Vitamin D deficiency in adults leads to osteomalacia—inadequate mineralization of newly formed bone matrix—weakening the skeleton and predisposing to pathological fractures. Vitamin D deficiency in children causes rickets. Fat-soluble vitamin absorption requires bile salts and intact small bowel mucosa; both may be compromised in Crohn disease. Vitamin K deficiency (D) would present with coagulopathy, not bone fragility.
keypoints: ⭐ Fat malabsorption → vitamin D deficiency → osteomalacia (adults) or rickets (children)
Crohn disease can impair absorption of all fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
⭐ Osteomalacia features inadequate bone mineralization and pathological fractures
Vitamin K deficiency presents with coagulopathy (prolonged PT/INR), not bone disease

questions.stem: A homeless man, who is a chronic alcoholic, is brought to the hospital in a wasted state. He is noted to have a peripheral neuropathy, difficulty balancing, and dementia. He dies suddenly of an arrhythmia, and at autopsy, lesions are found in the mamillary bodies and the vicinity of the third ventricle. The vitamin deficiency associated with these signs and symptoms is which of the following?
questions.explanation: This patient has classic Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome combined with beri-beri, both caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Thiamine deficiency in chronic alcoholics results in encephalopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and cardiovascular manifestations (wet beri-beri). The pathognomonic autopsy finding is atrophy of the mamillary bodies with loss of ganglion cells and rupture of small blood vessels. Vitamin B12 (B) deficiency causes macrocytic anemia and subacute combined degeneration of the cord. Niacin (D) deficiency causes pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia).
keypoints: ⭐ Thiamine (B1) deficiency in alcoholics causes Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome: encephalopathy + peripheral neuropathy
Wernicke encephalopathy pathology: mamillary body atrophy, third ventricle lesions
⭐ Beri-beri = thiamine deficiency: wet (cardiac) or dry (neurologic) forms
Niacin deficiency → pellagra (3 Ds: dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia)

questions.stem: A starving, 4-year-old, African boy presents with apathy, generalized edema, and an enlarged fatty liver. The physician notes that, despite generalized growth failure, subcutaneous fat is preserved. What is the appropriate diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency in a diet relatively high in carbohydrates. Key features include: edema (from hypoalbuminemia), enlarged fatty liver, apathy, skin depigmentation, and relative preservation of subcutaneous fat (unlike marasmus). It typically occurs in children weaned to protein-poor diets. In contrast, marasmus (C) is caused by total caloric deprivation and presents with profound wasting of both fat and muscle, without edema. The other choices represent specific vitamin deficiencies (beri-beri = B1, pellagra = niacin, scurvy = vitamin C).
keypoints: ⭐ Kwashiorkor = protein deficiency: edema, fatty liver, preserved subcutaneous fat
Marasmus = total caloric deprivation: muscle and fat wasting, NO edema
⭐ Kwashiorkor edema is caused by hypoalbuminemia (protein loss → low oncotic pressure)
Fatty liver in kwashiorkor results from impaired lipoprotein synthesis due to protein deficiency

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl is examined at a clinic in central Africa. Physical examination reveals wasting of muscle and fat, and a protuberant abdomen. Her pulse, blood pressure, and temperature are low. The face appears wrinkled. There is no evidence of generalized edema. What is the appropriate diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Marasmus results from deficiency of all dietary elements—total caloric deprivation. Clinical features include profound wasting of both muscle and subcutaneous fat (no preserved fat as in kwashiorkor), a wrinkled face resembling a 'shrunken old person,' protuberant abdomen, and low vital signs. Crucially, there is NO edema (distinguishing it from kwashiorkor). Immune impairment leads to recurrent infections. If untreated, these children fail to reach adult stature. The other choices represent specific nutritional deficiencies without the pan-deficiency pattern.
keypoints: ⭐ Marasmus = total caloric deprivation: profound muscle AND fat wasting, NO edema
Key distinction: marasmus has no edema; kwashiorkor has edema (hypoalbuminemia)
⭐ Wrinkled, 'shrunken old person' appearance is characteristic of marasmus
Marasmus causes immune deficiency, recurrent infections, and permanent growth failure
